assessment_method: Local original-resolution multimodal visual inspection using judge-v4-source-fidelity-style-transfer; one actual assessment per case.

cases.expected_relation: Identical style truth and candidate produce near-zero style, color, composition, and technical loss.
evidence: Candidate is byte-identical to the style truth, so the visible layout, palette, contour treatment, texture, and rendered detail are unchanged.
Source-fidelity and semantic fields are recorded as zero for this style-only control and are not the relation under test.

cases.expected_relation: Identical source truth and candidate produce near-zero source_fidelity and semantic loss.
evidence: Candidate is byte-identical to the source truth, retaining all visible identity/content, entities, pose, geometry, markings, and scene relations.
Style, color, composition, and technical fields are recorded as zero for this source-only control and are not the relation under test.

cases.expected_relation: The unstyled source retains low source_fidelity loss while receiving high style and color loss against the style truth.
evidence: Candidate is the same photograph as the source truth, so its subject, clothing, pose, surrounding objects, and visible markings are preserved.

Candidate lacks the reference's illustrated ink contours, flat graphic color fields, abstract poster layout, dry-brush marks, and printed-paper treatment; its photographic palette and rendering differ strongly.
The photo itself is coherent and has no evident corruption, so technical loss remains low.

cases.expected_relation: The assessment should identify the large cross-domain visual mismatch in either display order; component direction is not comparable after labels are deliberately reversed.
evidence: In both presentations, the two images visibly differ between an illustrated graphic poster and an unstyled photograph.
The deliberate label reversal does not change the detected cross-domain mismatch magnitude in this calibration control.
